Record a job starting, so the queue shows what is in flight before it finishes and a second actor can see it.

With --scope set this is a claim: if another open job already holds that scope, this fails with 409 naming who holds it, what they are doing, and since when -- so you can pick up something else instead of duplicating the work.

The summary is prose describing the work, never the command that performs it.

Usage:
  erun jobs start [flags]

Examples:
  erun jobs start --type fix --issue sophium/erun#2109 --scope sophium/erun#2109 \
    --summary "fixing the jobs claim race" --actor erun/code4

Flags:
      --actor string          Who is doing the work: the orchestrator id or agent identity
      --actor-kind string     What kind of actor this is: agent, orchestrator, or human (default "agent")
      --dry-run               Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --environment string    Local environment name this work runs in (omit for host-side work)
  -h, --help                  help for start
      --issue string          The issue this work belongs to, e.g. owner/repo#2109
      --local-job-id string   The in-pod job id this mirrors, when there is one
      --scope string          What this job claims, so a second actor is told who holds it
      --summary string        What the work is, in prose (not the command that performs it)
      --type string           Job type: fix, review, gate, release, deploy, investigate, plan, triage, or maintenance

Global Flags:
      --erun-alias string   erun platform cloud alias to target (defaults to the sole configured erun-type alias)
      --output string       Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time                Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count       Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
